_note: The keyboard map this session ships, and the single source of it. iarch-keybinds renders .config/hypr/generated/keybinds.lua from this file plus the differences a person has saved in ~/.config/iarch/keybinds.json, so a bind is written here or in that file and nowhere else. Until Part 5 the direction was the other way round -- tools/extract_keybinds.py read this record out of .config/hypr/keybind.lua -- and the reversal is the point: a report about a file cannot be edited, because the next extract overwrites the edit, which is why the Shortcuts page was read-only. Every spelling a bind here may use is recorded in data/design/keybinds.json against the pinned compositor, and iarch-keybinds check validates this file against that record rather than against an assumption.

action.lua:
function()
    local window = hl.get_active_window()
    if not window then
        return
    end
    if window.floating then
        hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.move({ x = -30, y = 0, relative = true }))
    else
        hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.swap({ direction = "left" }))
    end
end
action.why_lua: Asks the compositor whether the focused window is floating and picks one of two dispatchers. The v1 bind answered the same question by running `hyprctl activewindow -j | jq -r .floating` through bash and grepping for the string true, which needed two external programs to ask a yes-or-no question the Lua API answers with a boolean field (LuaBindingsQuery.cpp:129-138, LuaWindow.cpp:101-102).

The `=` in --min-value=1 is not a style choice either: the option is declared optional_argument, so a separate word is never consumed and would be taken for the operation. Arch builds the package with `make ENABLE_SYSTEMD=1`, which is the build whose non-root `set` falls back to logind's Session.SetBrightness (brightnessctl.c:217-228 and :371-395), so the key needs no root, no setuid bit and no `video` group.
